tweets: Calling external contracts can transfer control to another contract before your function finishes.
This allows a malicious contract to call back into you, creating multiple invocations that interact undesirably.
The core risk is that state changes happen after the call, not before.
To prevent this, perform all internal state updates before making any external calls.
This approach is known as the Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern.
Alternatively, you can use a reentrancy lock like OpenZeppelin's ReentrancyGuard.
